subject: Private Offer — signature path and procurement timeline (CloudNova)
message_1_subject: Private Offer — signature path and procurement timeline (CloudNova)
message_1_body:
Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Following up with the private-offer options we discussed — we want to align on the buyer approval path so AWS activation doesn't get held up by multi‑BU signoffs. High level: 

Option A (single-signature): 1 private offer, CFO or central procurement signs for all BU consumption. Activation window: immediate upon signature. Term suggestion: 12 months (standard).

Option B (staggered/BU-specific): separate private offers per BU, each requires its own procurement and CFO approval. Activation staggered by BU; we typically see a ~4–6 week drift per additional BU. Term suggestion: 24 months with phased activation.

To help your team decide, can you confirm: 
- who on the CloudNova side must sign (name/title and whether they can sign for all BU)?
- procurement timeline target for offer execution?
- any standard evidence pack requests (SOC2, network diagrams, IP/BCP) we should attach to the private offer?

I attached a short mutual action plan and a sample PO draft for your legal team to review. If CloudNova prefers a single private offer but with delegated approvers (AWS supports an approver roster), that’s an option and could avoid staggered activation.

If helpful I can loop in Finance to discuss discounting tradeoffs for longer term (e.g., 24 months).

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
message_2_subject: Re: Private Offer — signature path and procurement timeline (CloudNova)
message_2_body:
Jonas — thanks for the summary and attachments. A few clarifications from procurement and legal: 

1) Signatory: our CFO (Rohit Malhotra) can sign for multi‑BU contracts but procurement needs explicit evidence up front (SOC2 Type II report, data residency statement, and network topology). Our engineering security lead will require the SOC2 and a short summary of what data is retained in logs.

2) Timeline: target is to execute by July 15 to line up with our Q3 budget. That means we need final PO language, evidence pack, and a confirmed approver roster by July 1.

3) Term preference: CFO prefers 24 months with an annual renewal clause (financial prefers longer to lock pricing). Can Redwood offer a modest discount for 24 months? Also our legal has a standard clause for marketplace offers — we may need an MWBE/DEI clause included.

4) Co-sell entitlements: our GTM lead asked whether co-sell listing (AWS co-sell) can be included as part of the activation so we can start joint leads post-activation.

Attaching our procurement evidence checklist (see inline). Can you confirm you have a single private-offer flow that supports a delegated approver list? If not, we’ll need separate offers.

Best,
Asha Patel
Head of Procurement, CloudNova
asha.patel@cloudnova.com
message_3_subject: Re: Private Offer — signature path and procurement timeline (CloudNova)
message_3_body:
Asha — great, thanks for the details. Quick answers: 

• AWS private offers do support an approver roster (delegated approvers) so we can create a single offer and list multiple authorized signers. That will keep activation immediate after the authorized signer signs.

• Evidence: attaching the index we usually send (SOC2 Type II, data flow diagram, retention matrix). I’ll flag the SOC2 and a one‑page network diagram for your security lead.

• Term & discount: we can propose two pricing rows in the PO: 12 months (baseline price) and 24 months (~8% discounted unit price). Vanessa, can you confirm whether finance is comfortable with an 8% concession for 24-month committed usage?

• Co-sell: yes — we can start co-sell enablement as soon as the offer is active; there’s a short seller registration step with AWS and a joint GTM folder we’ll share.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Redwood to send a revised PO that includes delegated approver roster and both pricing rows.
2) Redwood to upload evidence index to the HubSpot deal and share a short link.
3) CloudNova to confirm signatory names and target July 1 for approver roster.

I’ve attached a PO draft with the two pricing rows and a short evidence index. If that looks good we’ll push to DocuSign and AWS private-offer once your CFO signs.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
